1) packages/forge-adapters/src/comment-on-issue.shared.test.ts
================================================================================
Command: node --experimental-strip-types --test packages/forge-adapters/src/comment-on-issue.shared.test.ts
Result: ℹ tests 19 / ℹ pass 0 / ℹ fail 19  (every test in the file runs its body and fails on
behavior — none are load/import failures)

Summary tree (all 19 cases fail; each is a real behavioral assertion, not a placeholder pass):

▶ commentOnIssue shared spec
  ▶ github
    ✖ POSTs { body } to the comment endpoint with the same per-kind auth headers as the sibling methods
    ✖ treats any res.ok (2xx) response as success, not only a hard-coded 201
    ✖ non-OK HTTP response rejects with "commentOnIssue: <kind> responded <status>", after exactly one fetch
    ✖ an unparseable issue_url rejects without calling fetch (not merely notImplemented)
    ✖ a pull/MR web path in issue_url is unparseable and must not fetch
  ▶ gitlab  (same 5 cases, all ✖)
  ▶ gitea   (same 5 cases, all ✖)
  ✖ github: always POSTs to api.github.com regardless of a custom baseUrl option or the pasted issue host
  ✖ gitlab/gitea: the API origin comes from the constructor baseUrl option, never from the issue_url host (SSRF)
  ✖ gitlab: a nested-group namespace is encodeURIComponent-ed as a single :id segment in the notes URL
  ✖ the same body string is sent verbatim as the JSON { body } field for every kind
ℹ tests 19 / ℹ pass 0 / ℹ fail 19

================================================================================
2) apps/server/src/writeback.test.ts
================================================================================
Command: node --experimental-strip-types --test apps/server/src/writeback.test.ts
Result: ℹ tests 15 / ℹ pass 6 / ℹ fail 9

Full test tree:

▶ issue #14 write-back (commentOnIssue on 认领 / 提交PR / 完成)
  ▶ 认领 (claim) write-back
    ✖ imported gitea task: REST claim posts a write-back comment with the task credential, not the agent key
    ✔ native task: REST claim never posts a write-back comment and writes no 回写 event
    ✖ imported github task: claim posts to the GitHub Issues API with a Bearer task-credential header
    ✖ imported gitlab task: claim posts a note with a PRIVATE-TOKEN task-credential header
    ✔ a forge 5xx on the claim comment never blocks the claim, and no successful 回写 is recorded
  ▶ 提交 PR (submit_pr) write-back
    ✖ imported gitea task: MCP submit_pr posts a write-back comment containing publicId, PUBLIC_URL, and pr_url
    ✔ a forge network failure on the submit_pr comment never blocks submit_pr, and no successful 回写 is recorded
  ▶ 完成 (complete) write-back
    ✖ imported gitea task: pollPendingReviews posts a write-back comment on 已完成 (merged)
    ✖ imported gitea task: a webhook merged delivery posts a write-back comment on 已完成
    ✔ imported gitea task: a closed (unmerged) PR via pollPendingReviews (已退回) never posts a completion write-back comment
    ✔ a forge 5xx on the completion comment never blocks reaching 已完成, and no successful 回写 is recorded
  ▶ native task: no write-back at any of the three hooks
    ✔ a native task never posts a write-back comment across claim, submit_pr, and completion
  ▶ retry (retryPendingWritebacks, exported from apps/server/src/poller.ts)
    ✖ re-posts a write-back comment that failed on 认领, and does not duplicate once it has succeeded
    ✖ re-posts a write-back comment that failed on 完成 (via pollPendingReviews)
    ✖ is a safe no-op when there is nothing pending

Note: the 6 passing cases are all "must NOT comment / must NOT block" negative-space assertions
that are vacuously true today (the feature doesn't exist, so of course nothing comments) and
remain true once correctly implemented — they are not false positives, they pin required
non-behavior (native tasks, 已退回, and non-blocking-on-failure).

Failure #1 (claim never posts, github kind):

      at TestContext.<anonymous> (.../writeback.test.ts:1034:14)
  (asserts `typeof poller.retryPendingWritebacks === 'function'`; today it is `undefined` because
  apps/server/src/poller.ts exports no such function. This assertion is reached and fails cleanly
  — the dynamic `await import('./poller.ts')` inside the test body means this missing export does

  and produces its own independent behavioral RED, as shown above.)
